# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

## From cand_0002 (tau2 airline, tools capability)
- The prompt's per-task FAILURE summary phrases the gold `action_checks` arguments as
  "agent used cabin='economy'…". That is MISLEADING: the arguments in `action_checks` are
  the EXPECTED/gold action, not what the agent did. I nearly designed a fix around the
  wrong values before opening the raw trace. Suggest relabeling to "expected action" (and
  noting `action_match=false` just means no matching agent call was found).
- The prompt heavily pushes "fix behavioral misses in CODE," but on this benchmark the
  dominant failures are the agent CONFIRMING then not issuing a write, or transferring
  instead of acting — tool code cannot force a call the model omits. A short caveat that
  some behavioral clusters are only addressable structurally (composite that collapses the
  action) or not at all from the tool surface would set expectations and save iterations.
- REMOVE_TOOLS is honored by the adapter (filters `get_tools`) but the mechanism lives in
  a repo far from the working dir and isn't referenced near `tools.py`. A one-line pointer
  in the seed comment ("filtered in adapters/adapter.py at the get_tools boundary; methods
  stay callable for delegation") would let the optimizer trust removal without hunting.
- It would help to state the `reward_basis` (here DB × COMMUNICATE, action_checks
  informational) in the task prompt. Discovering that action names don't affect the score
  is the single most important fact for choosing safe edits, and it currently requires
  parsing reward_info by hand.
